=== Possible John Glasco in Irish rosters, 1798–1799 ===
John Glasco is PRESENT at the Black-Rock Association meeting 8 May 1798.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1214061848/ The Public Register, or, Freeman's Journal, 1798-05-29, p.4].</ref>

John Glasco appears in the 24 September 1799 roster, continued beneath an earlier COUNTY OF LONDONDERRY heading.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1214179229/ The Public Register, or, Freeman's Journal, 1799-09-24, p.2].</ref>

The two entries retain separate identities: the 1798 Black-Rock attendee is not proved to be the 1799 County Londonderry roster bearer. A shared surname and county do not establish relatives.

This may concern [[Glasgow-4090]]. Possible 1799 Desertoghill contemporary, born before 1772; no roster link.

=== Possible John Glasgow, Allegheny Township list in Huntingdon County context, 1799 ===
John Glasgow is named under Allegheny Township in a township-grouped list accompanying Huntingdon County election-meeting material.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/587806805/ The North American (Philadelphia), 1799-09-10, p.3].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1140587856/ Pennsylvania Weekly Telegraph (Oracle of Dauphin and Harrisburgh Advertiser), 1799-09-18, p.2].</ref>

The two issues repeat one list. Allegheny Township was then in Huntingdon County and later in Cambria County, so the county labels are compatible. The list does not establish a father-and-son relationship with a 1790 household head.

This may concern [[Glasgow-4090]]. Broad uncertain before 1772 birth permits adulthood; Irish locality statement supplies no migration or individual connection to this record.

=== Possible John Glasgow, Carlisle postal addressee, 1793 ===
John Glasgow, care of William Brown, Esq., is an addressee in the Carlisle post-office list headed 1 January 1793.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1033763029/ The Carlisle Gazette, and the Western Repository of Knowledge, 1793-03-06, p.1].</ref>

"Care of William Brown, Esq." is the address qualification, not evidence of kinship. A postal entry alone does not establish that its addressee was alive on the list date.

This may concern [[Glasgow-4090]]. Broad uncertain before 1772 birth permits adulthood; Irish locality statement supplies no migration or individual connection to this record.

=== Possible John Glasgow, Millrig labourer and Kirkliston subscription, 1798 ===
John Glasgow, labourer, Millrig, is named among voluntary subscriptions in the parish of Kirkliston.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/601860386/ The Edinburgh Advertiser, 1798-07-20, p.6].</ref>

This is a named labourer at Millrig in Kirkliston parish. It does not connect him to the Irish Johns, the Carlisle addressee or the Allegheny list.

This may concern [[Glasgow-4090]]. Broad uncertain before 1772 birth permits adulthood; Irish locality statement supplies no migration or individual connection to this record.
